# Pettifer

## Overview

- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v2 c1 P3](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0003), [v2 c1 P4](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0004)</sub>
- **Origin:** New Brunswick  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- **Role:** Farmer  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** A crank  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>

## Appearance

His house is situated in front of a thick grove of spruce.

_Sources: [v2 c3 P0](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0000)_

## Personality

He is an eccentric, stingy, and quick-tempered individual who lives alone and explicitly dislikes having women near his premises. Despite his explosive temper and occasional sudden fits of anger, he can be surprisingly gentle, courteous, anxious, and sheepish once calmed down. He is stubborn regarding his domestic habits and maintains a strong skepticism towards local affairs, ministers, and community gossip.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P1](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0001), [v2 c1 P3](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0003), [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P6](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0006), [v2 c1 P8](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0008), [v2 c3 P1](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0001), [v2 c3 P3](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0003), [v3 c11 P50](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0050)_

## Abilities

- Farm work and handling livestock  <sub>[v2 c1 P3](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0003), [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>

## History

After moving to Brierley from New Brunswick, Mr. Pettifer bought the former Bell farm next to the Abernethy home. He quickly earned a local reputation as an eccentric bachelor, eschewing regular meal times, washing his dishes all at once in a rainwater hogshead only on wet Sundays, and refusing to donate money to local church stipends or missionary efforts. He employed John Henry Carter as a farmhand, though he provided irregular meals and criticized his clumsiness. On one occasion, after mistaking his Jersey cow's antics for crop damage, he burst furiously onto the Abernethy property, only to later receive Nell's confession that she had mistakenly sold his stray cow for twenty dollars. Though upset, he managed his temper and restrained his ill-mannered parrot, Nutmeg. Later, Nell confided in him about her ambitions to write a short story, which he received with skepticism, expressing that too much rubbish was already being published.

## Background by volume

- Hails from New Brunswick  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- Purchased Robert Bell's farm in Brierley to the west of the Abernethy property  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- Received a talking parrot named Nutmeg from his seafaring brother  <sub>[v2 c3 P6](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0006)</sub>

## Quotes

> Ignore that parrot. He . . . he utters foolishness constantly. My brother, a seafaring man, gave him to me. A sailor's speech isn't always particularly refined, and birds like parrots copy things easily.  <sub>[v2 c3 P6](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0006)</sub>
